alerts.title: DTG-associated hyperglycemia and pre-diabetes
alerts.message: Guidelines state that clients with 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycemia and high baseline glucose should not be initiated or transitioned to DTG. Hyperglycemia has been reported among HIV patients on DTG. This patient has multiple risk factors: age ≥30, family history of DM, and BMI ≥25. At TLD switch 18 months ago, fasting glucose was 92 mg/dL (normal), so DTG was permissible with glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year. Now fasting glucose is 118 mg/dL and HbA1c 6.1%, both in pre-diabetic range. Evidence for drug attribution: DTG is temporally associated with rising glucose, and guidelines acknowledge DTG-related hyperglycemia. Evidence against: family history of DM and acanthosis nigricans suggest intrinsic insulin resistance. No glucose monitoring over the past 18 months is documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess whether DTG should be continued given pre-diabetes progression. If continued, monitor fasting glucose and HbA1c every 3 months. Consider switching to ATV/r or EFV400 per guidelines.

alerts.title: Significant weight gain and obesity on DTG
alerts.message: Guidelines identify obesity as a preventable disorder increasing risk of heart disease and diabetes. This patient gained 17 kg in 18 months on TLD (65 kg to 82 kg), with BMI rising from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m², now classified as obese. Waist circumference 96 cm and acanthosis nigricans indicate central adiposity and insulin resistance. DTG is temporally associated with this rapid weight gain. Evidence against drug attribution: sedentary lifestyle and dietary factors may also contribute. The weight gain is compounding her pre-diabetes and dyslipidemia. No plan addresses weight management or lifestyle modification today.

evidence.recommended_action: Initiate lifestyle modification counseling including diet and physical activity. Consider DTG contribution to weight gain and evaluate regimen alternatives if weight gain continues.

alerts.title: Dyslipidemia with adverse lipid profile
alerts.message: Guidelines note that dyslipidemia is a risk factor for diabetes development in PLHIV and that antiretroviral drugs are a major cause of metabolic complications. This patient's lipid profile is markedly abnormal: total cholesterol 228 mg/dL, LDL 148 mg/dL, HDL 38 mg/dL, and triglycerides 212 mg/dL. This atherogenic pattern, combined with new hypertension (BP 138/88), obesity, and pre-diabetes, significantly increases cardiovascular risk. DTG and TDF can contribute to lipid changes, though TDF is generally lipid-neutral. No baseline lipid panel is available for comparison. No plan addresses lipid evaluation or management.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate dyslipidemia per cardiovascular risk stratification. Consider dietary intervention and statin therapy if indicated. Repeat lipid panel to confirm trend.

alerts.title: Missing glucose monitoring per DTG guidelines
alerts.message: Guidelines require glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year when initiating or transitioning clients with 2 or more hyperglycemia risk factors to DTG. This patient had 3 risk factors (age ≥30, family history of DM, BMI ≥25) at TLD switch 18 months ago. No interim glucose or HbA1c results are documented in the 18 months since transition. Had monitoring occurred, pre-diabetes might have been detected earlier. The clinician's plan today is blank, with no glucose monitoring or diabetes screening scheduled.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule fasting glucose and HbA1c every 3 months. Complete a full DM screening assessment and document a management plan addressing pre-diabetes.
